subject.title: Feature: config option to route gateway lifecycle warnings to a dedicated channel

question: Should OpenClaw add a dedicated warning-routing config for gateway lifecycle and internal tool-error messages, and should it be catch-all, category-based, suppression-only, or handled through the existing `messages.suppressToolErrors` path?
rationale: The code already has partial suppression, but a destination router adds new shared config and can change where safety-relevant warning messages appear for existing channel workflows.

options.title: Design default-compatible routing
options.body: Approve a new warning-routing contract with current behavior as the default, explicit target parsing, docs, and tests for lifecycle, tool-error, and existing suppression paths.

options.title: Use suppression only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` and narrower channel fixes as the supported operator path, and close or narrow destination routing as out of scope.

options.title: Split by warning class
options.body: Keep this issue for lifecycle routing only and move tool-error final/off semantics to the existing related issue.

recommendation.title: Design default-compatible routing
recommendation.body: Approve a new warning-routing contract with current behavior as the default, explicit target parsing, docs, and tests for lifecycle, tool-error, and existing suppression paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across the shared dispatch, routing, and tool-error visibility surfaces that would carry the product decision into code.
